forest.new_sub: An empty forest: a master index, the dialect, and its own git history.

overview.start_ask: Ask a question in plain language
overview.no_model: No model is bound to this forest yet, so Ask cannot answer. Everything else works.
ask.title: Ask the forest
ask.sub: Retrieval runs inside your scope first; only then does the bound model read what it found.
ask.placeholder: Ask anything about what is in this forest…
ask.evidence_hint: Every id below was actually read to produce this answer. Click one to open it.
ask.nothing: Retrieval found nothing inside your scope for that question.
ask.no_model: No model is bound to this forest for answering yet.
ask.ex3: Summarise what is under the largest branch.
ask.depth_hint: More nodes means a better-grounded answer and a slower, costlier call.
ask.limits: Answers are read from node text. A question whose answer is an aggregate over dataset rows is refused rather than guessed — use Data for those.
ask.hops_hint: Instead of one deterministic sweep, the model holds the primitives and navigates — locate, look, move, pick — until it can answer. Costs one model call per hop.
ask.material_hint: The summary decides which node; the body is what the model was given. These are the exact snippets and sections.
ask.material_outline: Outline only — the body exceeded the per-node budget
ask.path_clocks: Per hop: the forest call + the model turn that chose it.
ask.working_hops: Foraging — searching, reading, deciding where next…
ask.stage_entry: entry search over curated metadata and bodies
ask.stage_walk: hopping: one model call per decision
ask.stage_write: writing the answer from what was read
explain.cost_unknown: This provider publishes no price, so the cost is unknown — not zero.
ask.hybrid_hint: Fuses the vector layer into the search that finds the material. Off by default: on our corpora it pushed the right node off first place. Turn it on to measure that on yours.
explain.title: How this ran
explain.sub: Every call the answer made, and what each one cost.
explore.title: Explore
explore.edges_hint: Only trails whose other end is within your scope are listed.
explore.leaf: A leaf: nothing below it and no trails out within your scope.
playground.title: Playground
playground.sub: The same calls an agent makes, with the same budgets. Nothing here is a simulation.
playground.locate: locate — find entry points by curated metadata
playground.move: move — the trails from a node
playground.answer: answer — retrieval plus the bound model
playground.terms_hint: Literal words, comma separated. No regular expressions.
playground.curl_hint: Same route, same key, same rules your applications get.
playground.mcp_hint: Point any agent harness at {url} as a streamable-HTTP MCP server with this key, and it gets these calls as tools.
playground.empty: Run a call to see what comes back.
data.sub: Reading goes through query (read-only, one statement at a time). A change is one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE through tend — shown to you first, then committed on its own.
data.empty_hint: Its tables appear underneath it, and the first one opens with its rows already loaded.
data.insert_hint: Every box only takes what its column stores. An empty one means NULL, and you read the INSERT before it runs.
data.needs_value: This column does not accept NULL.
data.needs_datetime: A complete date and time is needed.
data.pending: These are the {n} statement(s) tend will run. Nothing is written until you apply them.
data.partial: {done} of {total} statements were already applied when the error hit. The grid was reloaded with the real state.
data.edit_hint: Double-click a cell to edit it, or use the bin to drop a row. Changes stay on screen — highlighted, reversible — until you save them.
data.no_rowid: This table has no rowid, so no row can be addressed on its own: reading only.
data.read_only: You may read this dataset. Editing rows needs the tend capability.
data.structure_note: Structure is read-only here. tend never accepts DDL (spec C.10): a table is born with plant’s declarative schema and changes by being rebuilt.
ingest.title: Add documents
ingest.sub: Files become forest: converted, summarised, linked and committed — the same pipeline the command line uses.
ingest.drop: Drop files or a folder here
ingest.drop_hint: Markdown, text, CSV, JSON, Word and Excel. Tabular files become queryable datasets.
ingest.pick_folder: Choose a folder on this computer
ingest.dest_hint: An existing branch. Everything lands under it.
ingest.path_hint: Read with the Station’s own filesystem access, which is why this needs the admin capability.
ingest.running: Ingesting — this can take a while with a model bound…
ingest.sync_hint: Re-reads the folder you last mirrored and updates only what changed.
ingest.curated: The ingest model wrote {n} summary(ies) and {regions} region summary(ies).
ingest.curated_partial: {n} document(s) fell back to a derived summary.
ingest.curated_trimmed: {n} were trimmed to fit the summary budget.
ingest.model_silent: The ingest model never answered, so every summary fell back to the text itself. Nothing was lost — but nothing was curated either.
ingest.model_rejected: The ingest model answered, but its summary was rejected {n} time(s) and every summary fell back to the text itself. This is a model, prompt or token-budget problem, not a connection one.
ingest.model_empty_hint: An empty reply usually means a reasoning model spent its whole token budget thinking. Raise max tokens for this binding, or pick a model that answers directly.
ingest.uncurated: No ingest model is bound, so summaries were derived from the text itself. That works — binding one makes them better.
ingest.needs_cap: Adding documents needs the ingest capability.
models.title: Models
models.sub: A forest is not one workload. Choose who summarises what comes in, and who answers what goes out.
models.providers_sub: Any OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint: OpenRouter, LiteLLM, vLLM, a local llama.cpp.
models.name: Name
models.key_hint: Stored server-side and never sent back to this page. Leave blank to keep the stored one.
models.env_locked: Declared by the environment. Change the variables and restart the Station.
models.env_note: Providers marked “from the environment” come from this deployment’s own variables. Their key is read from the environment when a call is made and is never stored in the registry.
models.role_ingest_sub: Writes the summary every later search navigates by. Worth a careful model — it runs once per document.
models.role_answer_sub: Reads retrieved material and writes the reply. Worth a fast one — it runs on every question.
models.max_tokens_hint: The whole reply the model may write, not the summary length. Too low truncates the reply mid-JSON; a reasoning model needs room to think first.
models.scope_note: Binding a model does not widen access. Retrieval runs inside the asker’s scope first, so the model only ever reads what that person could already read.
models.needs_admin: Choosing models for this forest needs the admin capability.
access.title: Access
access.sub: A person’s world is exactly what you grant here — everything else is not merely hidden, it does not exist for them.
access.you_sub: What you are holding right now.
access.who_ph: A name or a service id, for example alice
access.forests_hint: Tick every forest this access covers. One person, one decision — not one visit to this form per forest.
access.forests_same_level: The level and scope below apply to all {n} forests.
access.forests_drop_all: No forest is ticked — saving removes this person’s access entirely.
access.forests_mixed: This person currently holds a different level or scope on different forests. Saving levels every ticked forest to the choice above.
access.scope_multi: Several forests are ticked, so this grant covers each of them whole. Branch names are not shared between forests — tick a single forest to choose branches.
access.scope_no_branches: This forest has no branches below its root.
access.scope_pick_hint: Pick branches below. Anything not picked simply does not exist for them.
access.advanced_hint: Deviating from the role is allowed — the role is a starting point, not a cage.
access.preview_line: {who} will see {scope} of {total} branch(es) in {forest}, and will be able to {can}.
access.preview_cannot: They will not be able to {cannot}.
access.preview_none: Choose at least one branch, or they will see nothing at all.
access.issue_hint: Shown once. Only its digest is stored, so it cannot be recovered later.
access.key_warn: Copy it now — this is the only time it is shown.
access.no_people: Nobody else has access to anything yet.
access.needs_admin: Managing access needs the admin capability on this forest.
access.needs_admin_hint: Ask whoever gave you this key. Below is what your own key holds.
role.reader_desc: Can read what you choose. Nothing else.
role.analyst_desc: Reads, and runs read-only SQL over datasets.
role.editor_desc: Reads and queries, and can create and edit nodes and dataset rows.
role.curator_desc: Everything an editor can do, plus loading new documents in.
role.owner_desc: Full control, including giving access to other people.
role.custom_desc: A capability set you chose by hand.
audit.title: Audit
audit.sub: Reads are recorded here; writes are commits in the forest’s own git history. Neither records content.
audit.needs_admin: Reading the audit log needs the admin capability.
audit.no_bodies: Arguments are stored as a digest, never in full: the log records access, not content.
nav.tokens.blurb: Which credentials exist, and until when
gate.password_hint: The super-administrator is configured in the Station environment; other people are given one under Tokens.
tokens.title: Issued tokens
tokens.sub: Every key that can reach this Station through the API — with what it is for, when it dies, and when it was last used.
tokens.new_sub: A token carries the permissions of the person it belongs to. It does not have permissions of its own.
tokens.for_hint: Only people whose forests you fully administer appear here.
tokens.label: What it is for
tokens.label_hint: A token nobody can identify is a token nobody dares revoke.
tokens.never_warn: A token that never expires is only as safe as everywhere it has ever been pasted. Prefer a date and renew it.
tokens.once: Copy it now — only its digest is stored, so this is the only time it is shown.
tokens.inherits: This token will be able to do exactly what {who} can do, in exactly the forests {who} was granted. To change that, change their access.
tokens.none_hint: Issue one above to let an application, an agent or a script reach this forest.
tokens.needs_admin: Managing tokens needs the admin capability.
tokens.needs_admin_hint: You can still use the key or the login you already hold.
tokens.password_sub: A password only decides how someone proves who they are. What they may do is still decided by their access.
tokens.new_password_hint: Leave blank to remove the password and leave only the token door.
tokens.password_set: {who} can now sign in with a password.
tokens.env_note: The super-administrator lives in the Station environment (MONKEYLLM_STATION_ADMIN / _PASSWORD) and is never stored here — rotate it there and restart.
access.levels_sub: What each level means, so choosing one does not require leaving this screen.
access.levels_note: A level is a starting point: any grant can deviate from it, and the scope you pick narrows it further.
models.model_ph: Search or type a model id…
models.model_hint: {n} model(s) offered by this provider. You may still type one it does not list.
models.model_none: This provider advertises no model matching that.
models.model_test_first: Choose a provider to load the models it serves.
models.model_stray: This provider does not advertise that model. Fine if you know it exists — but a model id from another provider is the usual cause.
nav.pin_hint: The star pins a shortcut to the bar below.
nav.pin_full: The bar holds {n} — remove one first.

people.title: People
people.sub: Everyone who can reach the forests you administer — their level, their scope, and how they get in.
people.new_sub: Access, sign-in and a token — one form, because it is one decision.
people.edit_sub: Everything about this person, in one place.
people.not_manageable: They also hold a forest you do not administer, so their credentials are out of reach.
people.none_hint: Add someone to give them access, a way in, and a token if they need one.
people.who_hint: A person or a service. This name appears in every audit record and cannot be changed later.
people.give_password: Let them sign in with a password
people.password_hint: Optional. Without one they can still use a token.
people.password_clear_hint: Leave blank to remove the password and keep only the token door.
people.token_hint: For scripts, agents and integrations. Shown once.
people.partly_applied: Some of it was applied; the rest was refused:
people.needs_admin: Managing people needs the admin capability.
people.needs_admin_hint: Your own access is shown under Overview.
gauntlet.title: Meaning-based navigation (the Gauntlet)
gauntlet.sub: Orders the neighbours the forager sees by closeness to the question, instead of by past usefulness.
gauntlet.optional: Entirely optional. Without an embedding model bound, every call behaves exactly as it does today — not degraded, identical.
gauntlet.model_hint: An embedding model, not a chat model. Changing it invalidates the index and forces a rebuild.
gauntlet.mismatch: The index was built by a different model than the one bound now, so it is being ignored. Comparing vectors from two models does not rank badly — it ranks meaninglessly. Rebuild to use it again.
gauntlet.build_hint: Embeds each node’s title and summary — not its body. Runs once; later edits refresh themselves.
gauntlet.toggle_hint: Off shows the ordinary order, so you can compare the two on this corpus.
gauntlet.not_here: The Gauntlet has no switch here: it orders what a forager sees while hopping, and this console asks one question instead of navigating. Try it under Playground, on look or move.
gauntlet.enabled_hint: Off leaves the model bound and the index built, and every call behaves exactly as it would without either.
integrations.locked: The deployment manual needs the admin capability.
integrations.overview.title: How it fits together
integrations.overview.sub: One container, three surfaces, the same governed forests.
integrations.overview.p1: The Station wraps the untouched MonkeyLLM engine with identity, per-forest policy and audit. Every surface routes through the same enforcement seam — there is no unscoped path, so whatever this console shows, an API client holding the same key could fetch too.
integrations.overview.p2: One image, two volumes, no external database: the Studio is a static bundle built into the image, and the host registry is a single SQLite file. All three surfaces authenticate with the same API keys, checked at a single gate.
integrations.install.title: Install and run
integrations.install.sub: From a clean checkout to a running Station — in Docker or straight on a machine.
integrations.install.docker_p: The compose file at the repository root builds one image and runs it with named volumes, so a crash, a rebuild or an update never loses data. The console is served at the root of the same port.
integrations.install.bootstrap: The first boot mints a bootstrap admin key with full capabilities and prints it exactly once — only its digest is stored. Save it before the logs rotate.
integrations.install.source_p: Install the engine and the Station, build the console once, and serve. The --writable flag accepts writes; without it the Station refuses them up front with E_READONLY — reads always work.
integrations.install.first_p: Creating a forest through the API requires admin on an existing one, so on an empty volume the first forest is born with the engine’s own CLI inside the container. From then on, forests are created from the console — no shell needed again.
integrations.deploy.title: Deploy in a container
integrations.deploy.sub: What persists, how to put it behind a domain, and how updates behave.
integrations.deploy.volumes_p: Everything worth keeping lives in named volumes — the container itself is disposable:
integrations.deploy.vol_forests: Every forest: markdown, its embedded git history, dataset payloads, derived caches.
integrations.deploy.vol_registry: The host registry: principals, API-key digests, grants, audit — one SQLite file.
integrations.deploy.vol_models: GGUF weights for the optional local inference sidecars — multi-GB, kept out of the image.
integrations.deploy.dok1: Create a Compose service from this repository and point it at deploy/docker-compose.dokploy.yml.
integrations.deploy.dok2: Set the environment variables you use — the annotated catalogue lives in .env.example.
integrations.deploy.dok3: Add your domain pointing at the station service, container port 8800, HTTPS on.
integrations.deploy.dok4: The first deployment’s logs print the bootstrap admin key once. Store it.
integrations.deploy.dok5: Create the first forest through the container terminal, exactly as in the install section.
integrations.deploy.local_llm_p: No external LLM provider is needed: two llama.cpp sidecars ship behind compose profiles. The first start downloads the weights into the models volume; later starts reuse them. Leave the embedder off to keep entry search on its BM25-only contract.
integrations.deploy.updates_p: Redeploy or rebuild at will — the image is replaced, the volumes are untouched, and work continues where it was. For backups, snapshot each forest as a git bundle and copy the registry volume with it: grants and key digests belong with the forests they govern.
integrations.deploy.readonly: Remove --writable from the command line and redeploy for a read-only Station: reads keep working, and writes, ingest and forest creation are refused up front with E_READONLY.
integrations.mcp.title: MCP — plug an agent in
integrations.mcp.sub: The same forests, spoken in the protocol agents already use.
integrations.mcp.p1: Add the Station to any MCP client as a streamable-HTTP server with an Authorization header. The tools are the engine’s primitives plus answer, so an agent that works against a local vine serve works here unchanged — gaining only a key and a scope.
integrations.mcp.first_call: Have the agent call forests() first: a scoped key has no master index, and that call returns the roots to start from. Anything outside the key’s scope reports E_NOT_FOUND, exactly as a missing node does.
integrations.mcp.client_json: JSON configuration — Claude Desktop and compatible clients
integrations.mcp.hosts: The MCP surface only answers hosts listed in MONKEYLLM_STATION_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Serving through a domain or a changed port means naming that host there — or * to skip the check; every request still needs an API key.
integrations.tool.forests: Lists the forests this key may use, with capabilities and starting roots.
integrations.tool.locate: Ranked entry points over curated metadata — where to drop into the forest.
integrations.tool.look: Cheap digest of one node: summary, edges, children, stats.
integrations.tool.move: Neighbours of a node along typed edges.
integrations.tool.pick: Reads the body, or one section of it.
integrations.tool.scan: Filters a branch’s nodes by metadata.
integrations.tool.sniff: Literal search inside bodies — the facts summaries do not carry.
integrations.tool.harvest: One-shot retrieval: ranked evidence with exact snippets, no hops.
integrations.tool.answer: A grounded answer written by the model bound to the forest, with its evidence.
integrations.tool.query: Read-only SQL against a dataset node.
integrations.tool.ingest: Puts documents into the forest through the Gardener.
integrations.api.title: REST API
integrations.api.sub: Everything this console does travels through these routes — there is no privileged side-channel.
integrations.api.auth_p: Send the key as a bearer token on every request. A login with username and password returns a session token — an ordinary key with a 12-hour life — so past the door there is exactly one authorization path.
integrations.api.pattern_p: One route shape covers every primitive: POST the arguments as JSON to the primitive’s name. Responses honour explicit token budgets — a cut result always says truncated, never cuts silently.
integrations.api.errors_p: Failures are one envelope mapped onto HTTP codes, and the hint is written for the caller — show it. Out of scope is indistinguishable from absent: a node the key may not see reports E_NOT_FOUND, byte for byte.
integrations.route.health: Liveness, and whether the password door exists.
integrations.route.login: Exchanges username and password for a 12-hour session token.
integrations.route.me: Who this key is: principal, admin flag, grants.
integrations.route.forests: The forests this key may use, with the roots to start from.
integrations.route.call: The primitives, plus answer and ingest, per forest.
integrations.route.admin_forests: Creates a forest: empty index, dialect, its own git history.
integrations.route.people: Person-shaped governance: grants, password and tokens in one form.
integrations.route.keys: Lists, issues and revokes API tokens.
integrations.route.grant: Binds a principal to forests with capabilities and branch scope.
integrations.route.audit: The read log: who saw what — digests only, never bodies.
integrations.route.providers: Inference providers; the test route checks an endpoint before saving.
integrations.route.models: Per-forest model bindings by role: ingest, answer, embed.
integrations.route.canopy: The optional vector layer: build, enable or disable per forest.
integrations.access.title: Keys and access
integrations.access.sub: How identity, capabilities and tokens govern all three surfaces.
integrations.access.p1: A grant binds a principal to a forest with capabilities and branch-prefix scope: allow and deny lists of subtree prefixes, deny wins, and no grant means no access. A token carries the permissions of the person it belongs to and has none of its own — what a token can do is answered by that person’s access, never by the token.
integrations.access.roles: The role presets under Access are shorthands over exactly these capabilities — the API speaks capabilities only.
integrations.access.keys_p: A token is shown once at issue; the Station stores only its digest. Expiry and revocation are enforced inside the single authentication gate every surface passes through, so a revoked token dies everywhere at once. Issue and revoke under Access, or over the admin routes.
integrations.access.breakglass_p: Set both variables and the console offers a password form for a super-administrator compared against the environment and never stored. Rotate it by changing the variable and restarting. Without the variables there is no password door at all — the only safe default.
integrations.access.audit_p: Reads land in the host registry: principal, forest, primitive, an argument digest, size and timestamp — never bodies. Writes are git commits inside the forest, stamped with the principal, and the commit id returned to the caller is the stamped one.
integrations.env.title: Environment reference
integrations.env.sub: Everything the container reads from its environment. The annotated catalogue lives in .env.example.
integrations.env.admin: Break-glass console login. Both must be set; never stored; rotate by restart.
integrations.env.hosts: Hosts the MCP surface answers. Add your domain, or * to skip the check.
integrations.env.port: Published port of the compose service — 8800 by default.
integrations.env.llm: Chat provider, pre-configured and read-only under Models; the key is never copied into the registry.
integrations.env.llm_model: Default model id, response budget and reasoning mode for that provider.
integrations.env.embed: Embedding endpoint and model for the optional vector layer. Unset keeps entry search on its BM25-only contract.
integrations.env.s3: S3-compatible endpoint for remote payloads — MinIO, R2.
